title: Grade 6 Science — Thu, May 21
description: Food: Where Does It Come From? — Day 4 of 5: Herbivores, carnivores, omnivores
subject: science

questions.question: A cow has flat, grinding teeth. This adaptation is suited for:
options: Grinding and chewing tough plant material like grass
questions.explanation: Herbivores like cows have flat molars for grinding cellulose-rich plant material. Their jaw moves sideways, unlike carnivores.

questions.question: A lion has sharp canine teeth and forward-facing eyes. These adaptations help it:
options: Hunt, kill, and tear flesh; and judge distance for pouncing
questions.explanation: Sharp canines tear flesh. Forward-facing eyes give binocular vision for depth perception — essential for judging pouncing distance.

questions.question: Humans have both sharp canines AND flat molars. This suggests humans are:
options: Omnivores — adapted to eat both plants and animals
questions.explanation: Our mixed dentition (canines for meat, molars for plants) reflects our omnivorous nature — evolved to eat both plant and animal food.

questions.question: The digestive system of cows is longer and more complex than that of lions because:
options: Plant cellulose is harder to break down than meat and requires longer digestion with special bacteria
questions.explanation: Plant cell walls (cellulose) are tough to digest. Cows have a 4-chambered stomach and host cellulose-digesting bacteria, making their system far more complex.

questions.question: Scavengers like vultures and hyenas eat:
questions.explanation: Scavengers consume carcasses of already dead animals. They play an important role in cleaning up ecosystems.

questions.question: Which food habit has the LOWEST environmental impact?
options: Eating only fish from the ocean
A plant-based diet (mostly vegetables, grains, pulses)
questions.explanation: Plant production requires far less land, water, and energy than animal farming. A mostly plant-based diet has a significantly lower carbon footprint.

questions.question: Bacteria in a cow's first stomach (rumen) help by:
options: Digesting cellulose (plant cell walls) that the cow itself cannot break down
questions.explanation: Cows cannot produce cellulase. Rumen bacteria ferment and break down cellulose in grass, allowing the cow to extract nutrition from plant cell walls.

questions.question: Eagles eat fish AND rabbits AND snakes. Eagles are therefore:
questions.explanation: Eagles eat only animals — fish, mammals, reptiles. Even though their diet is varied, eating only animals makes them carnivores.

questions.question: Bears eat berries, fish, honey, and insects. Bears are classified as:
questions.explanation: Bears eat both plants (berries, roots) and animals (fish, insects, small mammals) — making them omnivores.

questions.question: Why do carnivores have shorter digestive tracts than herbivores of similar size?
options: Meat is easier to digest and absorb than tough plant cellulose — no lengthy fermentation needed
Digestive length is unrelated to diet
questions.explanation: Meat is protein and fat — relatively easy to chemically digest. Plants contain cellulose requiring slow bacterial fermentation. Herbivores need longer intestines for this.

questions.question: Rabbits practice coprophagy (eating their own faecal pellets). Why?
options: Their first digestion is incomplete; re-eating soft faeces allows bacteria to further break down cellulose
Faecal pellets contain harmful bacteria they want to remove
questions.explanation: Rabbits pass two types of droppings. Soft cecotropes contain partially digested material with bacteria and vitamins — re-eating them allows complete extraction of nutrition.

questions.question: Sunflower seeds are eaten by birds. The birds are then eaten by cats. This is a food chain. The producer is:
questions.explanation: The sunflower plant makes its own food via photosynthesis — it is the producer. Seeds are part of the plant; the bird and cat are consumers.

questions.question: If all lions were removed from a savanna, what would most likely happen?
options: Deer/zebra population would explode, overgraze, and destroy the ecosystem
questions.explanation: Lions control herbivore populations. Without predation, deer/zebra overpopulate → overgraze → grassland destroyed → cascading collapse of the ecosystem.

questions.question: Which correctly classifies these animals: Deer, Wolf, Crow, Grasshopper?
questions.explanation: Deer eats plants; wolf eats meat; crow eats both (seeds, insects, carrion, small animals); grasshopper eats plants.

questions.question: A herbivore that can store water in its body (like a camel) is adapted for:
options: Desert environments with scarce water and plant food
questions.explanation: Camels can go days without water (stored as metabolic water from fat), eat dried thorny plants, and have wide feet for sand. These are desert adaptations.
